implemented: Service-only PostgreSQL request claims prevent concurrent or repeated provider calls for guarded requests; scope includes company, user, task and stable request key.
Guard enabled for Silvio chat, message-correlated classifier calls, daily briefing and memory extraction LLM calls. Other router clients are not automatically opted in.
Completed text responses are reusable without a second provider call or wallet debit. Cached tool-call responses require recovery and cannot silently repeat business actions.
Ambiguous network/stream outcomes and crashed workers are not automatically retried. No lease stealing or fail-open if the claim/checkpoint/completion store is unavailable.

Each guarded provider response is checkpointed with generation ID, model and known usage/cost before response validation or charging. Discarded paid responses remain visible separately from the company's single successful-call bill.
HTTP, JSON and SSE provider 402 errors stop model fallback. Persistent cooldown lasts 15 minutes per hashed API key. The briefing batch uses deterministic alerts after its first credit error.
Daily briefing delivery uses a deterministic per-company/user/day message ID and ignores duplicate inserts; save errors are no longer treated as successful deliveries.
Automatic briefings stop if company status cannot be read. Existing daily cron redacts expired response bodies after the seven-day replay TTL, retaining dedup tombstones.
Billing RPC JSON success=false or missing ledger ID is rejected, including HTTP-200 responses. No additional provider fallback after a billing failure.

Missing provider cost is explicitly classified as a tier estimate when complete token usage and valid tier prices exist. Missing cost and unavailable estimate are blocked, not recorded as a free success.
Ledger metadata records generation_id, original_idempotency_key, provider_request_key, cost_source and usage completeness. Commercial tariff formula is unchanged.
Precheck rejections use a separate tenant-scoped error key so a later funded retry cannot replay the zero-charge denial as its successful bill.

deployment_requirements.order: Review/apply migration before deploying any guarded caller. Also review existing uncommitted dependencies separately; do not overwrite other-terminal work.
deployment_requirements.fail_closed: Deploying the guarded edge functions without this migration blocks guarded provider calls. Frontend build alone does not activate server fixes.
deployment_requirements.shared_router_consumers: Need redeployment to receive common billing/402 changes; not deployed by this task.
deployment_requirements.history_reporting: For flow/iteration reports use coalesce(metadata->>'original_idempotency_key', idempotency_key). Guarded ledger keys are tenant-scoped digests.

historical_reconciliation.safety: No charge_ai_call retry, fabricated zero balances, historical inserts or wallet changes. Missing history does not prove that no debit happened.

remaining_limitations: Production has not been changed or benchmarked with these fixes.

A complete cross-worker request-cost total and shared spending cap still require correlation of embeddings, nested tool AI, delegated Council and background memory. Current turn metrics explicitly exclude them; this work does not claim a complete total.
Historical generations without generation_id cannot be reconstructed from the ledger alone. Provider/account evidence is required.
Uncertain requests deliberately require reconciliation. There is no automatic provider re-spend or automatic business-tool replay to recover a crashed worker.
The paid provider and wallet test fixtures do not replace a multi-connection production-like load test or a controlled paid latency benchmark.
The entire application test suite/typecheck was not certified by this targeted verification.
